minor.issue: sniff() in photos.py only validates magic bytes (first 8–12 bytes). A payload like b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n' + arbitrary bytes passes validation and gets stored; the browser then renders a broken img (naturalWidth=0). Real user uploads from Photos/Finder are unaffected. Consider PIL.Image.open(..).verify() for defense in depth.

Optional hardening: run uploaded image bytes through PIL.verify() in photos.py so garbage-after-magic uploads are rejected (defense in depth; current behavior is accept-and-store, UI shows broken image).
critical_code_review_comments: photos.py sniff() uses magic-byte-only validation; sufficient to prevent XSS/SVG abuse but accepts corrupt image payloads. Fine for an MVP; worth decoding on upload if production-grade.

CandidatePhoto.jsx silently swallows fetch errors (.catch(() => {})). If storage returns 502/404 after hasPhoto=true, user sees initials fallback with no indication. Acceptable UX; a log/console.warn would help debugging.
No rate limit on /candidates/{cid}/photo. An admin could flood uploads; low risk given admin-only but a rate_limit(user,...) would match the pattern used in voting/auth.
